lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-9054 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/rchen
EDUCATION
Harbor State University | B.B.A. in Finance | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Lakeside Golf Club | Caddie | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Caddied about 5 rounds a week, carrying bags and reading greens for members.
- Helped the pro shop run the weekend junior tournament.
Stonebridge Manufacturing | Financial Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jan 2023 - Jun 2025
- Improved close efficiency by 40% by automating reconciliations and intercompany eliminations.
- Modeled the capital plan for 12 plant projects in a shared NPV template, so every request used the same discount rate and payback rules.
- Wrote the variance commentary for the monthly board pack, explaining each line more than 5% off budget.
- Valued the acquisition target by discounting its free cash flow to equity at the company's weighted average cost of capital.
- Reported a 45% group EBITDA margin by adding the EBITDA margins of the three business units.
- Built the rolling 18-month cash-flow forecast for a USD 600M manufacturer, keeping monthly forecast error under 4% and letting treasury pay down USD 40M of revolver debt early.
Crescent Bank | Credit Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Dec 2022
- Underwrote 60 small-business loans worth USD 45M, and none of the approved loans defaulted in their first two years.
- Reviewed 3 years of declined applications; my findings changed two ratio thresholds and raised approvals from 41% to 48% with no rise in early defaults.
- Writes the covenant-monitoring checklist for the portfolio, cutting missed covenant tests from 7 to 1 a year.
- Built a spreading template for borrower financials that cut each credit memo from 6 hours to 3.
PROJECTS
Regional Utility Valuation | Independent Project | Excel | Nov 2024 - Present
- Valued a listed regional utility with a 10-year DCF and a comparable-company check, landing within 6% of the market price.
- Tested the valuation's sensitivity: a 1-point change in the discount rate moved the share value from USD 52 to USD 44.
- Shared the model and a two-page note with the university investment club, which used it in its spring pitch.
Student Investment Fund | Analyst, Team of 6 | Excel | Sep 2018 - May 2019
- Supported the FP&A team with financial reporting and analysis.
- Rebuilt the fund's performance report to show returns against its benchmark, which the committee used at every meeting.
- Built an 18-month cash forecast for a USD 600M business, holding error to about 4% and freeing USD 40M to repay debt early.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel, Bloomberg Terminal
Methods: financial modeling, DCF valuation, forecasting, credit analysis

items.says: Check that the profile link works and leads to a current profile.
Consider adding your location if you are applying outside Metro City.
Move the Lakeside role below the finance experience or into a separate section.
items.because: Its current position makes it the first experience a reader sees.

items.says: Use a tense consistent with an ongoing role.
Keep the five-rounds-a-week figure only if it reflects your typical schedule.
Show more impact than the duties alone convey.
items.because: The duties alone do not show much impact.

items.says: Specify your tournament responsibility or the tournament’s scale.
Define and explain how you measured the 40% close-efficiency improvement.
Clarify your ownership of the capital-plan modeling.
Say whether the standardized approach affected investment decisions, if applicable.
Indicate the scope or consequence of the board-pack commentary.
items.because: The bullet describes a task rather than its value.

items.says: Correct the acquisition-valuation methodology.
items.because: Free cash flow to equity is generally discounted at the cost of equity, while free cash flow to the firm is generally discounted at WACC.

items.says: Adding business-unit EBITDA margins does not produce a group margin.
items.because: The group margin must use appropriate consolidated EBITDA and revenue, accounting for eliminations.

items.says: Define how the under-4% forecast error was measured.
Avoid implying the forecast alone caused the early debt repayment.
items.because: The forecast should reasonably have supported that decision.

items.says: Clarify which approved loans had a full two-year observation period.
items.because: Readers may question the cohort and timing.

items.says: Explain the basis for linking your findings to the threshold changes.
Ensure the approval-rate comparison covers comparable periods.
Define the observation window for “no rise in early defaults.”
Change “Writes” to a tense matching the completed role.
Clarify whether seven missed tests falling to one is an annual comparison.
Specify whether the time saving applied to typical memos or a particular loan type, if relevant.
Reconsider using proximity to market price as the valuation’s result.
items.because: Being within 6% does not by itself demonstrate that the valuation was sound.

items.says: Be ready to defend the valuation assumptions.
State the direction and starting point of the discount-rate change.
items.because: Without them, the USD 52-to-44 sensitivity is hard to interpret.

items.says: Check that “spring pitch” aligns with the project dates.
Clarify what the investment club used from your work.
Verify that the FP&A work belonged to the student fund.
items.because: “FP&A team” sounds like a corporate role and conflicts with the project heading unless the fund had such a team.

items.says: Clarify your individual contribution to the performance report, if needed.
items.because: The project lists a six-person team.

items.says: Delete or relocate the student-fund cash forecast after verifying the facts.
items.because: It repeats the Stonebridge forecast’s scale, error, and debt outcome under a 2018–19 student project.

items.says: Correct the valuation-method bullet before listing DCF valuation as a strength.
items.because: The listed methods should be substantiated by the experience and projects above.
